shapes.label: Protocol / contract
shapes.one_sentence: Use when multiple producers and consumers need the same boundary semantics before richer tooling can stay honest.
best_for: public boundaries that many tools or services must agree on
interop or report surfaces that need stable field meaning
cases where examples alone are no longer enough
common_failure_modes: writing the contract after incompatible tools already shipped
pretending a hosted service contract is the same thing as general semantics
letting style preferences masquerade as hard protocol requirements
prefer_when: many actors need compatible field meaning
silent ambiguity would corrupt downstream interpretation
avoid_when: only one local tool exists and the semantics are still exploratory
a corpus or report surface would answer the actual need sooner

shapes.label: Evidence collector
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the first missing capability is preserving observable facts from builds, tests, intake, or execution rather than explaining them beautifully.
best_for: build-state, intake, coverage, inventory, or benchmark evidence
cases where facts disappear after the run unless explicitly recorded
required_artifacts: at least one verify or doctor path
common_failure_modes: jumping straight to dashboards without trustworthy capture
mixing imported truth and derived judgment into one opaque blob
collecting so much data that privacy or performance costs break adoption
prefer_when: the workflow currently loses facts after execution
later diff/report tooling is blocked on missing receipts
avoid_when: the problem is primarily recommendation or governance rather than fact capture
upstream already captures the needed truth sufficiently

shapes.label: Reference layer
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the job is to import bounded upstream truths and answer narrow queries, diffs, or routed views without owning all upstream semantics.
shapes.truth_location: imported source lanes plus bounded derivations
best_for: semantic context, migration/public API, adoption navigation
questions that need exact subject capture and explicit authority lanes
common_failure_modes: turning the layer into a universal knowledge graph
hiding freshness and partiality behind confident prose
confusing imported facts with final policy verdicts
prefer_when: multiple consumers need the same canonical imported truth
existing upstream sources are useful but fragmented
avoid_when: there is no stable enough upstream substrate yet
a local report command would answer the immediate workflow pain better

shapes.label: Report command
shapes.one_sentence: Use when users need local explainability close to the workflow, with low ceremony and clear linkage back to recorded facts.
shapes.truth_location: local machine state plus linked receipts
best_for: why did this rebuild, what changed, what ran, what failed, what drifted
explain surfaces that should live near Cargo or a companion CLI
required_artifacts: human-usable explanations linked to machine-usable artifacts
common_failure_modes: shipping pretty output with no link back to source facts
pretending local report output is a service API
adding commands before capture exists
prefer_when: the user pain is local workflow explanation
operators need answers without standing up a service
avoid_when: the main need is long-lived hosted aggregation across many orgs
the truth is still too unstable to expose even experimentally

shapes.label: Service surface
shapes.one_sentence: Use when shared hosting, centralized freshness, discoverability, or multi-user coordination are core to the value rather than incidental.
shapes.truth_location: hosted API, UI, or registry/service behavior
best_for: registry, docs hosting, shared dashboards, or centrally refreshed catalogues
cases where multi-user coordination or hosted availability is the product
common_failure_modes: building a hosted layer before local truth surfaces exist
confusing UI convenience with canonical semantics
shipping a service with no clear stewardship or abuse posture
prefer_when: centralized hosting materially changes what users can do
fresh shared visibility matters more than local-only explainability
avoid_when: a local collector or reference layer would solve the problem with less maintenance
the team cannot honestly staff a service

shapes.label: Corpus / atlas
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the missing capability is shared memory, comparison surfaces, defaults, anchors, or recurring cards rather than a new engine.
best_for: proving grounds, anchors, hypotheses, sources, defaults, lane maps
cases where future comparison depends on naming recurring units well
common_failure_modes: letting prose drift away from the maintained corpus
mistaking a corpus for proof of current truth
growing the atlas until it becomes unmaintainable
prefer_when: the repo keeps forgetting the same distinctions
future pilots or revisions need comparable named cards
avoid_when: the real problem is missing upstream evidence collection
a corpus would be empty theater without downstream use

shapes.label: Checker / validator
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the archive or toolchain needs a thin enforceable honesty boundary rather than another explanatory essay.
best_for: shared envelope honesty, corpus coherence, conformance fixtures
repo-level guardrails that future LLM edits can run
required_artifacts: positive and negative fixtures where appropriate
clear statement of what is and is not enforced
common_failure_modes: trying to validate semantics the checker cannot actually know
using a checker as a proxy for editorial judgment
adding hard rules without updating examples or protocol
prefer_when: a repeated structural failure can be caught mechanically
future maintainers need a fast trust-preserving pass
avoid_when: the disagreement is strategic rather than structural
the rule is too fuzzy to enforce honestly

shapes.label: Bridge / adapter
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the core value is connecting Rust to a foreign boundary, provider, toolchain, or native substrate without pretending to replace both worlds.
best_for: native-edge interop, foreign build handoff, toolchain/provider boundaries
specialist seams where host/target/provider truth matters
common_failure_modes: declaring a grand universal platform instead of a bounded bridge
erasing foreign-system truth under Rust-centric assumptions
mixing boundary mapping with policy judgment
prefer_when: the real blocker is crossing ecosystems or native boundaries
a reference layer still needs concrete adapters to be useful
avoid_when: the problem is really local evidence or recommendation rather than interop
the work would create a new runtime or build-system empire by accident

shapes.label: Pilot program
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the next honest step is a bounded proving lane with explicit scenarios, anchors, scorecards, and verdicts rather than a general launch.
best_for: new seam implementations that need comparable proof
cross-cutting experiments that should fail fast or graduate visibly
common_failure_modes: presenting a flattering demo as if it were representative
running a pilot with no graduate/deepen/fold/kill outcome
forgetting to name the non-claims
prefer_when: broad relevance is not yet proven
the archive needs comparable evidence before staffing more deeply
avoid_when: the work is already clearly a long-lived operating program
no realistic proving grounds or anchors can yet be named

shapes.label: Stewarded program
shapes.one_sentence: Use when the honest unit of work is a multi-asset, maintenance-heavy, funding-aware program rather than a single crate or binary deliverable.
shapes.truth_location: roadmap, staffing, governance, and coordinated assets
best_for: long-lived roadmaps, institution-facing initiatives, safety-critical or cross-language areas
cases where maintenance and governance dominate launch complexity
required_artifacts: relationship to component tools, corpora, or services
common_failure_modes: selling a maintenance-heavy program as one lightweight tool
launching without owners or funding posture
flattening many deliverables into one impossible product promise
prefer_when: the work spans multiple assets and teams over time
industry funding or governance alignment is part of the real plan
avoid_when: a smaller collector/reference/checker stack would already unlock the value
the team is using “program” language to hide vague scope
